title: Theater Five
paragraphs: ABC weekday anthology of short original radio dramas across crime, science fiction, suspense, social issues and other genres. Frozen GRH snapshot contains all 256 numbered broadcasts plus two undated reference tracks.
GRH documents the program through ABC weekday anthology run (August 3, 1964 to July 30, 1965) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Fred Foy (announcer on 240 recordings and director on 1 recording), Glenn Osser (conductor on 211 recordings, performer on 2 recordings, and composer on 1 recording), Jack C. Wilson (performer on 197 recordings, script editor on 181 recordings, and preparer on 15 recordings), Alexander Vlas-Daczenco (composer on 185 recordings, conductor on 2 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Ted Bell (director on 121 recordings, producer on 29 recordings, and executive producer on 20 recordings), Ed Blainey (performer on 111 recordings and sound technician on 109 recordings), and Lee Bowman (executive producer on 95 recordings and performer on 16 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.5e0945ef3ae9902a|WLS-FM]] (aircheck from station), and [[org|org.2291591a8979b4ab|WLS]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include youth and juvenile conflict, family and domestic crisis, crime and criminal investigation, war and military conflict, psychological tension and mental states, and science fiction and speculative technology.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Mid-1960s network-radio drama revival effort, Contemporary social issues in mid-1960s anthology drama, and Civil-rights-era social conflict.
